h1: The 8 Best 72-Inch Office Credenzas for Storage and Workspace, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 credenzas and sideboards around 72 inches wide, scored on build, cable access, storage layout and assembly effort.
summary: The HON 72-inch shell credenza in mahogany is the safest buy for a real office, with grommets for cables and metal-to-metal fastening. The Alera Valencia is the pick if you plan to add a return, bridge or hutch later. For a home office that needs doors and drawers instead of an open work surface, the 72-inch grooved-door sideboard and the soft-close black 71-inch cabinet are the strongest storage-first options.
intro: Most people shop for a 72-inch credenza by width and forget the other two numbers. A shell that is 24 inches deep and 29.5 inches tall behaves like a work surface. A sideboard that looks identical in a photo may be a kitchen-style buffet with doors that were never meant to hold a printer or a stack of binders. That difference decides whether the piece spends the next ten years as a working part of the office or as an expensive shelf.

This ranking separates the two families honestly. We reviewed eight pieces from their listings and spec sheets: five true 72-inch units and three 71-inch cabinets that occupy the same wall length. We scored them on construction, cable access, storage layout, how realistic the assembly is and what the maker tells you about load limits. Where a listing is silent on a number, we say so instead of guessing.

products.name: HON HONLCS7224LT1 72 in. Shell Credenza Mahogany, Brown
products.verdict: A no-nonsense 72-inch laminate shell with cable grommets and metal-to-metal fastening.
products.description:
This HON is a shell credenza: a 72-inch-wide laminate work surface on a frame, meant to sit behind or beside a desk and take a printer, a monitor or a stack of project files. It ships with desktop cable grommets, so a power strip can sit underneath and the cords can drop through the top instead of draping over the edge.

It takes first place because the construction details are the ones that decide whether an office piece survives years of moving and reassembly. Metal-to-metal fastening bites into steel rather than into particleboard threads, which is where most cheap credenzas fail the second time you tighten a bolt. The laminate surface is described as resistant to scratches, spills and stains, a sensible claim for a surface that will collect coffee rings and printer toner. Compared with the Alera, it gives up the stated option to add a hutch or bridge.

Buy it if you want a plain, durable 72-inch surface and plan to supply your own storage underneath or alongside. Skip it if you expect built-in drawers; a shell is just that, a shell.
cons: No hutch or bridge option listed
products.idealFor: Offices that want a durable 72-inch work surface behind the desk.
products.skipIf: You want drawers and doors built into the credenza.

products.name: Alera Valencia Series 72 by 24 by 29-1/2-Inch Credenza Shell, Mahogany Frame/Top
products.verdict: A commercial-grade shell that is built to grow into a return, bridge or hutch.
products.description:
The Alera Valencia is a 72 by 24 by 29.5 inch credenza shell with a commercial-grade worksurface and side panels. Its selling point is the Valencia system around it: the listing says it configures with a return, a bridge or a hutch, so it can start as a simple credenza and grow into an L-shaped or stacked workstation.

It ranks just below the HON because the HON lists the construction details a buyer can verify, and this listing leans on the system rather than the hardware. The upside is flexibility. If your office is likely to change in two years, a modular line saves you from replacing a credenza that no longer matches the desk. The tradeoff is that you are buying into one product family, and the add-on pieces are sold separately.

Buy it if you are furnishing an office in stages and want pieces that match. Skip it if the credenza will stay a standalone item, where the HON is the simpler call.
pros: Expandable with return, bridge or hutch
products.idealFor: Offices furnished in stages that need matching pieces.
products.skipIf: You only need one standalone credenza.

products.name: Hon Credenza with Knee Space, 72 by 24 by 29-1/2-Inch, Mahogany
products.verdict: The only unit here with a knee-space design, so you can sit and work at it.
products.description:
This HON uses the same 72 by 24 by 29.5 inch footprint as the shells but adds a knee-space design for direct seated use. The surface is multi-ply laminate, and the listing says it is rated to withstand boiling liquids, which matters if the credenza doubles as a coffee station.

It lands third because the knee opening costs you enclosed storage. If you intend to roll a chair under it and use it as a second workstation, that is exactly the right trade, and no sideboard here can do it. The price bracket is the highest in this ranking, and a buyer who only wants to park a printer on top is paying for a feature they will not use.

Buy it if the credenza will serve as a real workstation for a second person or a standing task area. Skip it if you want doors and drawers, or if the plain shell does the job for less.
cons: Highest price bracket in this list
products.idealFor: Two-person offices where the credenza is a second desk.
products.skipIf: You only need to hold a printer and files.

products.name: HON HONLCS7224LS1 72 in. Shell Credenza Slate Teak
products.verdict: The same sturdy HON shell in a cooler slate teak tone for modern rooms.
products.description:
The slate teak version of the HON shell shares the 72-inch width, desktop cable grommets and metal-to-metal fastening of the mahogany model. The only meaningful change is the finish, a grey-brown wood tone that sits better in contemporary offices than the traditional red-brown mahogany.

It ranks fourth because it is the same product as the number-one pick in a finish that fewer offices want. Dark mahogany suits conference suites and executive offices; slate teak suits open-plan and home studios. If your desk and shelves are cool-toned or grey, this is the right credenza and the mahogany one would clash. Otherwise, the ranking above it holds.

Buy it if your furniture is modern and the finish matters to you. Skip it if you already own a mahogany desk, or if you need drawers.
cons: Shell only, no storage built in
Same limits as the mahogany model
products.idealFor: Modern offices that want the HON build in a cooler tone.
products.skipIf: Your existing furniture is traditional mahogany.

products.name: 72" Modern Sideboard Buffet Cabinet with Vertical Grooved Doors
products.verdict: A full 72 inches of closed storage with a back hole for cables and a one-box delivery.
products.description:
This is a true 72-inch sideboard with vertical grooved doors, a cable management hole in the back and delivery in a single box. The listing puts assembly at about an hour and a half for two people, which is realistic for a cabinet of this size.

It ranks fifth because it is a home piece, not a commercial one. A sideboard hides clutter far better than a shell, and the back hole lets a router or charging strip live inside with the door closed. The cost is the construction standard: it does not carry the commercial-grade claims of the HON and Alera, so treat it as a home-office cabinet rather than a daily-abuse surface. It also needs a second person to build and hang the doors.

Buy it if the credenza is mostly for storing paper, supplies and tech out of sight. Skip it if you expect it to take heavy equipment or to be disassembled and moved often.
pros: Grooved doors give a modern look
products.idealFor: Home offices that want to hide supplies and cords.
products.skipIf: You need a commercial-rated work surface.

products.name: 71" Large Buffet Cabinet with 6 Soft-Close Doors and 2 Sliding Drawers, Black
products.verdict: Eight compartments, slow-close hinges and smooth slide rails in one inch under 72.
products.description:
This black 71-inch cabinet offers 8 compartments plus 2 sliding drawers, with soft-close hinges and smooth slide rails. The shelves adjust over a 2.5 inch range, which is enough to fit a ream box or a binder of a different height without wasting space.

It sits below the 72-inch sideboard because it is an inch narrower than the slug asks for, though for most walls that inch is invisible. The hardware is its strong point: soft-close hinges stop doors from banging in a quiet room, and sliding drawers are far easier on hands than a pull-out shelf. The tradeoff is the lack of any commercial claim and no stated load rating, so heavy items should stay on the lower shelves.

Buy it if you want the best day-to-day feel among the storage cabinets. Skip it if you need exactly 72 inches to fit a gap.
pros: Two sliding drawers for small items
products.idealFor: Quiet home offices that value smooth hardware.
products.skipIf: The gap you are filling is exactly 72 inches.

products.name: 71" Large Sideboard Buffet Cabinet with 3 Drawers and 6 Barn Doors, Black Wood
products.verdict: The only cabinet here that states its limits: 388 lb on top and 68 lb per shelf.
products.description:
This black wood cabinet has 3 drawers and 6 barn-door compartments, with a stated 388 lb countertop rating and 68 lb per shelf. It adds two center support legs on top of the corner legs, which is the right engineering response to a long span that would otherwise sag under weight.

It ranks seventh because the barn-door style is a look rather than a function, and sliding doors expose only part of a compartment at a time. The stated ratings are what earn it a place above the green model. A printer, a small monitor or a stack of boxes will not trouble a top rated for 388 lb. Be aware that, like the other cabinets, it is 71 inches, not 72.

Buy it if you plan to load the top with equipment and want numbers to rely on. Skip it if you dislike sliding doors that never open fully.
cons: Barn doors show half the shelf
products.idealFor: Offices placing printers or equipment on top.
products.skipIf: You want doors that swing fully open.

products.name: 71" Large Sideboard Buffet Cabinet with 6 Barn Doors and 2 Drawers, Green
products.verdict: A sage green and dark wood two-tone cabinet with 8 compartments and adjustable shelves.
products.description:
The green model pairs a sage and dark wood two-tone finish with 2 drawers and 8 enclosed compartments. There are two adjustable shelves, and the barn-door fronts give it a relaxed, residential look.

It finishes last because the listing offers no hardware or load detail beyond the layout, so you are buying on appearance. That is a legitimate reason when a room needs colour, and the compartment count is generous. Against the black soft-close cabinet it has less to say about everyday hardware, and against the barn-door sibling it has no stated weight rating at all.

Buy it if the credenza needs to look good in a creative studio or a living-room office. Skip it if you will put heavy equipment on top or need clear capacity figures.
pros: Suits studio or living room offices
products.idealFor: Creative spaces where colour matters more than specs.

methodology.title: Construction and fastening
methodology.description: We looked at fastening style, frame material and commercial-grade claims, since hardware is what separates a ten-year credenza from a two-year one.

methodology.title: Storage and layout
methodology.description: Drawer count, compartments, adjustable shelves and knee space were weighed against what a typical office needs to store.

methodology.title: Cable and equipment access
methodology.description: Grommets, back holes and the presence of a stated top load rating were scored for printers and power strips.

methodology.title: Assembly and delivery
methodology.description: Single-box delivery, assembly time and the number of people required were compared from the listings.

methodology.title: Value in the bracket
methodology.description: Features were set against the $200 to $500 and $500 plus brackets used throughout this ranking.

whatMatters.detail: A shell credenza is a work surface on a frame with no drawers, while a sideboard encloses storage behind doors. They solve different problems, so decide whether you need a place to put equipment or a place to hide supplies. The HON and Alera units are shells; the 71 and 72 inch cabinets are enclosed storage.

A 24 inch deep, 29.5 inch tall credenza sits at desk height and works as a return surface. Shallower cabinets look neat but may not take a standard printer. Check depth against your largest piece of equipment, and measure the gap behind your chair so you can still roll back.

Long spans sag unless they have center support, and particleboard stripping is the usual failure after a move. Metal-to-metal fastening, as on the HON shells, and center legs, as on the black wood cabinet, are the features to look for. Listings that mention neither deserve more scepticism.

Printers, chargers and routers all need power, and loose cords make a credenza look cheap. Desktop grommets, as on the HON shells, route cords through the top. A back hole, as on the grooved-door sideboard, lets power live inside a closed cabinet.

A stated rating tells you what the maker will stand behind. The black wood cabinet lists 388 lb on top and 68 lb per shelf, which is rare in this class. If a listing gives no number, assume the top is meant for light items only.

cards.text: A stated top load rating, center support legs and a way to route power. Depth should cover the printer's footprint with an inch to spare.

cards.text: The black wood barn-door cabinet lists a 388 lb top rating, and the HON shells give you grommets for cords. The grooved-door sideboard hides a power strip behind its back hole.

cards.text: The credenza is in a client-facing office, will be moved, or needs to act as a workstation. The HON shells, the Alera Valencia and the knee-space HON are built for that.

faq.q: Will a 72-inch credenza fit behind my desk?
faq.a: Allow 24 inches of depth plus at least 36 inches of walking or chair clearance. The shells here are 24 inches deep, so a room that is under about 5 feet between desk and wall will feel cramped.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a 72-inch credenza?
faq.a: Assuming every 72-inch piece is a work surface. Sideboards are shallower and lighter, and some are meant for dishes rather than printers. Check depth and any stated top load rating before you click.

faq.q: Is the HON worth it over a sideboard cabinet?
faq.a: If it will live in a business office, yes. The metal-to-metal fastening and commercial laminate are built to survive reassembly. For a home office that mainly stores supplies, a sideboard gives you more enclosed space for the money.

The grooved-door sideboard lists about an hour and a half with two people. Shell credenzas are simpler, though a metal frame and long laminate top still need a second person to hold the surface steady.

faq.q: How do I stop a long credenza from sagging?
faq.a: Keep heavy items near the legs, not in the middle, and use center supports if the model offers them. The black wood cabinet includes two center legs for this reason. Re-tighten fasteners after the first month, when the frame settles.

faq.q: Can I add a hutch later?
faq.a: Only on the Alera Valencia, which the listing says configures with a return, bridge or hutch. The HON shells and the cabinets are standalone, so pick the Alera if a modular setup is on your list.

finalTake: For a business office, the HON 72-inch shell in mahogany is the credenza to buy, with grommets, metal-to-metal fastening and a laminate that tolerates office abuse. Choose the Alera Valencia if you want to add a return or hutch later, and the knee-space HON if the credenza must double as a seated desk. For home use, the 72-inch grooved-door sideboard and the soft-close black cabinet are better at hiding clutter. Measure your wall and your printer before you decide.
